clue.text: Live Stone The Crows love song from the 60s

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
'stone the crows!' is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
both are terms of endearment for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A review praising a live set by the rock band Stone The Crows playing an old love song.
explanation.walkthrough: Stone The Crows was a real Scottish band, which is why the capitals look innocent; the phrase is also an old British cry of astonishment, the same as 'my!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ronettes' 1963 hit, produced by Phil Spector, is a classic romantic pop single of that decade.

clue.text: Tease about threat to career in demographic data

indicators.note: turning about means facing the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them

indicators.note: to career is to rush wildly out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mocking a statistician over a danger to their job prospects, buried in population figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun meaning a job, but it is the verb meaning to hurtle about.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of live births per thousand people each year is a standard population statistic studied by demographers.

clue.text: Professional work at the end of term?

definitions.text: Professional work at the end of term?

parts.words: Professional work at the end of term?
parts.note: surface reading: a job done as a school or university term closes, like marking exams
setter's reading: the term is a pregnancy, and its end is childbirth, where a trained professional assists

explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' suggests the academic calendar; a pregnancy that goes its full length is also said to reach term.
explanation.definitionFit: The trained profession of helping women through labour and delivery happens precisely when a pregnancy's full course is complete.

clue.text: Stall the pair patrolling entrance to Olympia

indicators.note: patrollers walk around an area, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: both refers to the two of a pair

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is where you enter it, its opening letter

parts.note: Olympia starts with O

explanation.surface: Two security guards walking round a trade stand at the doors of the Olympia exhibition hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Olympia is a large exhibition centre in London, which suits the stall of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a small stand or kiosk at a fair or exhibition, the same thing as a stall.

clue.text: Abuse King or 2 Kings?

parts.note: to boo is to jeer, a form of verbal abuse
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A question of whether one monarch or two are being insulted.
explanation.walkthrough: '2 Kings' looks like a number of monarchs, but it is the name of a part of the Old Testament; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Second Book of Kings is one of the named books of the Bible, so it is an example of the thing.

clue.text: IBM Melbourne could produce figures contact needs

indicators.note: producing something from raw material means reworking it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the company name and the city, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: The computer firm's Australian office could turn out the digits a client wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' looks like sales figures for IBM; it means digits, and the contact is a person trying to reach you by phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone wanting to reach you on your cellphone needs that string of digits, the personal telephone code.

clue.text: Distant relative phoned during off-campus university function

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the Open University teaches by distance learning, with no campus for students
rang is the past tense of ring, to telephone
tan is the tangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A faraway cousin rang in the middle of a university event held away from the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is the UK's distance-learning university, abbreviated OU; 'distant' in the definition echoes it neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: The great ape is a primate cousin of humans, but a more remote one on the evolutionary tree than chimpanzees.

clue.text: Island, the leader in after-hours entertaining business?

definitions.text: Island, the leader in after-hours entertaining business?

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island
biz is informal shorthand for business, as in showbiz

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: after-hours begins with A

explanation.surface: Asks which island leads the way in late-night clubbing and entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the answer is the island famous for its all-night club trade, and the question mark admits the loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balearic holiday destination in the Mediterranean is renowned worldwide for its nightclubs, a leader in that late-night trade.

clue.text: Remove first person in Strasbourg to squat in European court

indicators.note: squatters occupy a building from inside, so one piece settles within another

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
CT is the abbreviation for court
je is French for I, the first person singular, and Strasbourg is in France

explanation.surface: Evicting a Frenchman who has occupied a European court building, fitting as Strasbourg hosts European institutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person' suggests the leading individual; it is the grammatical first person, in French because of Strasbourg.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone is to throw them out or force them away, which is to remove them.

clue.text: Lovely short percussion instrument

indicators.note: falling short means stopping before the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a belle is a lovely, a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: Praise for a pretty little drum or chime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lovely' is read as a noun here: a lovely, like a belle, is a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck instruments sounded by hitting are percussion, and a bell is rung by striking its metal cup.

clue.text: Method of communicating with satellite is cool

parts.note: rad is slang for excellent, cool
Io is a moon, or natural satellite, of Jupiter

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic endorsement of talking via a satellite link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satellite' suggests a man-made one in orbit for signals, but it is a natural moon; the pieces run in the opposite order to the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending messages by electromagnetic waves through the air is a long-established way of transmitting information.

clue.text: Significant pair of musical works, back-to-back with common ending

indicators.note: sharing an ending means the join overlaps, so a letter they share is written only once

parts.note: the first of the pair is an opera, a musical work for the stage; its final A is the shared ending, written once

indicators.note: standing back to back means facing opposite ways, so the second runs backwards

parts.note: the second of the pair: the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Peron

explanation.surface: Two important compositions played one after another with the same finale.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair are an opera and the musical Evita; Evita turned round ends in A as the opera ends in A, and that shared A is written once.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'the operative word', the adjective means the key or most important one, hence significant.

clue.text: Earl breaks upper leg cycling some distance up

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece goes within another
a cycle goes round and round, so letters move from the front to the back in turn

parts.note: the thigh is the upper part of the leg
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: An aristocrat breaks his thigh while out cycling, perhaps on a hill some way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' reads as riding a bicycle; here it moves the leading T to the back, and the earl then breaks in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A height is an altitude or elevation, the measure of how far above the ground something is.

clue.text: Outrageous old woman drained nurses

indicators.note: to nurse a baby is to hold it in your arms, so one piece cradles another

parts.note: a drained battery or a drink gone still is flat
gran is a grandmother, an old woman

explanation.surface: A shocking scene: a spent elderly lady caring for nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like the people who get nursed; it is a verb, and the drained word does the holding.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagrant offence is glaring and shameless, so conspicuously bad that it is outrageous.

clue.text: Outline book of accounts unwrapped

indicators.note: unwrapping takes off the outer covering, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: a ledger is the book in which accounts are kept

explanation.surface: Sketching out an accounts book that has just been taken out of its packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outline' looks like a verb meaning summarise, but it is a noun: the boundary line of a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The edge of a shape is its boundary or rim, the contour that traces round it.

clue.text: Great man relaxed with a new novel

indicators.note: something novel is fresh and original, so the letters take an unfamiliar arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A great writer unwinding with a fresh novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book to relax with; it is an adjective meaning new, telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great, the Macedonian conqueror, is known by that title, so he is literally the great man.

clue.text: Quality testimonial at first

indicators.note: coming first means standing at the front, so this piece is placed ahead of the other

parts.note: taken as written
a testimonial is a tribute paid to someone

explanation.surface: Good quality is what a reference letter should speak of at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' reads as 'initially'; it means the little word goes first, ahead of the tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a characteristic or trait someone has, which is what a quality is.

clue.text: Mechanical process available to repair recalled clutches

indicators.note: calling something back brings it back the way it came, so it runs backwards
whatever is clutched is held inside, so the answer lies within the letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A garage's routine for fixing recalled vehicles that have faulty clutches.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about cars: a recall and a clutch, so the solver looks for a motoring word.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by rote means mechanical repetition without understanding, a routine done automatically.

clue.text: Undertakings question case for tortuous checks

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it back or restrain it, so one piece holds another
a case is the outer shell of something, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: tortuous begins with T and ends with S
to question is to ask

explanation.surface: Queries about promises in a convoluted legal case under review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tortuous' sounds like the legal word tortious, which suits 'case'; here only its outside letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work taken on, a job someone commits to doing, so both are jobs.

clue.text: Funny routine drinking beer with companion in cabin

indicators.note: a drinker takes liquid in, so one piece swallows another

parts.note: a skit is a short comic sketch
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A comedy double act drinking beer with a friend in a log cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: The companion is the CH of the Order of the Companions of Honour, a British honour; it goes before the beer inside the sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet at a ski resort is a wooden mountain hut, a type of cabin for holidaymakers.

clue.text: My cousins played recorders

indicators.note: playing with something means moving it about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Family members performing on those wooden school flutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorders' looks like the woodwind instruments, but it means a firm that records music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese-owned label is a major record company that makes and releases music recordings.

clue.text: Country type working to secure living at last

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held inside another
a working machine has moving parts, so the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: last means the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: living ends in G

explanation.surface: A rural sort of person with a job so they can finally earn a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country type' reads as a rustic person; the first word is the definition and the second is the raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a nation in north-east Africa, a sovereign state and therefore a country.

clue.text: Added time pressure no longer felt?

parts.note: ex- means former, something no longer so
tension is stress or pressure

explanation.surface: Once a deadline is pushed back, the stress melts away.
explanation.walkthrough: Tension that is no longer felt is former tension, hence ex-tension; the question mark flags the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra time granted beyond a deadline or at the end of a match is an extension of the period allowed.

clue.text: Loud crowd threatening a seafaring group

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a lot is a group or crowd, as in 'that lot'
ill can mean ominous or threatening, as in ill omen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy, menacing mob confronting a band of sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Ill in the sense of threatening is the one in 'ill wind' or 'ill omen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships or boats travelling together, a group at sea.

clue.text: Assume old temple can be made out

indicators.note: to make out a sound is to catch it by ear, so the word is judged by how it is heard

parts.note: fane is an archaic word for a temple

explanation.surface: Guessing that the ruins in the distance belong to an ancient temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assume' looks like 'suppose', but it means put on, as in assuming an air of innocence.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign an emotion is to put it on or pretend to it, just as one might assume a false manner.

clue.text: Half of relatives must support hard-working animal charity

indicators.note: taking half leaves only part, so the back three letters of six are dropped
in a down clue a support sits underneath, so this piece comes below the other

parts.note: an ox is a draught animal used for heavy work
one's family is one's relatives

explanation.surface: Relatives are obliged to fund an animal-welfare charity for working beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal charity' looks like one phrase; the animal belongs to the wordplay and the charity alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxfam is a large British-founded international aid organisation that relieves poverty, a well-known charity.

clue.text: Mark is catty — suffering iron deficiency?

indicators.note: a deficiency is a lack, so the symbol for the metal goes missing from the word

parts.note: catty in its literal sense, cat-like, is feline

explanation.surface: Mark is being spiteful: could anaemia be to blame?
explanation.walkthrough: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron; 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A line is a mark drawn or scored on a surface, a long narrow stroke.

clue.text: Norton, Gloucestershire: remote and agricultural, principally meat

indicators.note: principal means chief or first, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letters of the county, remote and agricultural
ham is cured pork, a meat

explanation.surface: A village of Norton in Gloucestershire, an English county, is described as isolated farmland, raising mostly livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norton, Gloucestershire' reads as a place name; Norton is the surname of the TV chat-show host.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Norton is an Irish television presenter, so the forename is what goes with his surname.

clue.text: Minister's raised staff attempt to dispose of dead

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something turns it to read from the bottom up

parts.note: a bar is a rod or staff

indicators.note: disposing of something throws it away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A cleric's raised crook in a bid to bury the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious leader and teacher, a minister of the faith to a congregation.

clue.text: Name what 15 26 9 made first

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to give a name to, as in what shall we name the baby
second meaning: the first telephone conversation, made by the inventor in 1876

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references spell out Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone, who made the first one to his assistant Watson.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone is to dub or term them, and a phone conversation is the other meaning of the word.

clue.text: Introduction to Leeds United fanzine stirred up disorder

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are jumbled
an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: Leeds begins with L
U is the abbreviation for United in football team names
taken as written

explanation.surface: A supporters' magazine for the football club Leeds United whipped up trouble among fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' suggests crowd trouble, which suits the football surface; it is a medical disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Influenza is a viral illness, and an illness or ailment of the body is a disorder.

clue.text: Government proposals seek money from society

parts.note: to bill someone is to send them a demand for payment
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Ministers' plans that aim to raise taxes from the public.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a single political statement; the definition is the first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Draft laws put before parliament for debate are called bills, the legislation a government proposes.

clue.text: See 5
Tablet to be swallowed in advance, round or oval

indicators.note: turning round means facing back the other way, so the whole runs backwards
whatever is swallowed goes inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: to cite is to advance or put forward as evidence
a pill is a tablet of medicine

explanation.surface: Instructions to take a pill beforehand, whether it's a round one or an oval one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round or oval' reads as two tablet shapes; 'round' is the turning signal and only 'oval' is the definition. The pill goes between the T and E before everything is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Elliptic describes the shape of an ellipse, an elongated closed curve, which is what an oval shape is.
